'''''Melica uniflora''''', commonly known as '''wood melick''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of grass in the family [[Poaceae]] that is native to much of [[Europe]], and to parts of [[South West Asia]] and [[North Africa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/mono/poa/melic/meliuni.html|title=''Melica uniflora'' (Den Virtuella Floran)}}</ref>

==Description==
The species [[rhizome]]s are elongated. The [[culm (botany)|culms]] are {{convert|20|–|60|cm}} long with leaf-blades being of {{convert|5|–|20|cm}} in length and {{convert|3|-|7|mm}} wide. The leaf-blade bottom is pubescent, rough and scaberulous. It has an open [[panicle]] which is both effuse and elliptic and is {{convert|6|–|22|cm}} long and {{convert|1|–|12|cm}} wide. The main branches have 1–6 fertile spikelets which are located on lower branches which are also scaberulous. Spikelets do ascend and have pedicelled fertile [[spikelet]]s. Pedicels are {{convert|2|–|5|mm}} long and are straight. The fertile floret [[lemma (botany)|lemma]] is both chartaceous and elliptic and is {{convert|5|–|7|mm}} long. Lower [[Chaff|glumes]] are oblong and are {{convert|3|–|6|mm}} in length. Flowers have 3 [[stamen|anthers]] which are {{convert|1.5|–|2.3|mm}} long with the [[fruit]]s being {{convert|3.5|mm}} long. The fruits are also ellipsoid and have an additional pericarp with linear [[hilum (biology)|hilum]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kew.org/data/grasses-db/www/imp06205.htm|author1=W.D. Clayton|author2=M. Vorontsova|author2-link=Maria Vorontsova (botanist)|author3=K.T. Harman|author4=H. Williamson|title=''Melica uniflora''|publisher=GrassBase|work=The Board of Trustees, [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|Royal Botanic Gardens]]|location=[[Kew]]}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
Swedish naturalist [[Anders Jahan Retzius]] described the wood melick in 1779.

==Distribution and habitat==
The species can be found in such Asian countries as [[Iran]] and [[Turkey]] and in European ones such as [[Balearic Islands]], [[Faroe Islands]], [[Finland]], [[Iceland]], [[Moldova]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], and [[Sweden]]. Also it was recorded in [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]] and [[Tunisia]].<ref name=herbarium>{{cite journal|url=http://herbarium.usu.edu/Meliceae/Melica/Melica_uniflora.htm|author=Verlag Paul Parey|title=Melica uniflora|year=1992|journal=Illustrierte Flora von Mitteleuropa|place=[[Berlin]] and [[Hamburg]], Germany|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807155803/http://herbarium.usu.edu/Meliceae/Melica/Melica_uniflora.htm|archive-date=2011-08-07}}</ref>

==Ecology and habitat==
The species is growing on plains and on elevation of {{convert|950|m}} in the [[Black Forest]] and on elevation of {{convert|1200|m}} in [[Alps]]. It can be found in hardwood forests near ''[[Beech|Fagus]]'' species. It also grows in dry and moist [[woodland]]s, which can either be acidic or neutral. Sandy or rocky soils are also common for such plants, but they need to be deep and loany as well. It grows on loamy soils in the north, while prefers decalcified soils in the south. The species is identical to ''[[Fagatalia]]'' which can be found in the [[Fagetum]] lowlands and also in the [[Carpinion]]. It rarely occurs in the [[Quercion]] clusters. Flowers bloom from May to July. Mostly, [[ant]]s feed on the species [[caryopsis]].<ref name=herbarium/>

==''Melica uniflora'' in cultivation==

''Melica uniflora f. albida'' has been awarded the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s '[[Award of Garden Merit]]'.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Melica uniflora f. albida {{!}}  Grass Like/RHS | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/74809/melica-uniflora-f-albida/details | access-date=2025-08-06 | website=www.rhs.org.uk}}</ref>

==''Melica uniflora'' in culture==
In the 19th century it was engraved on the illustration by [[Jacob Sturm]] in the book ''Deutschlands Flora in Abbildungen nach der Natur mit Beschreibungen'' which was published in [[Nuremberg]] in 1862.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.istockphoto.com/vector/melica-uniflora-and-common-quaking-grass-antique-flower-illust-gm184088508-16630147|title=''Melica uniflora''|date=25 May 2011 |publisher=I Stock Photo|access-date=January 27, 2019}}</ref>
